expectations.evidence: Document mentions NATO SECRET and NATO RESTRICTED (line 192) but does not list the full NATO classification hierarchy (NATO RESTRICTED, NATO CONFIDENTIAL, NATO SECRET, COSMIC TOP SECRET). No mention of COSMIC TOP SECRET or NATO CONFIDENTIAL as classification levels.

Line 51: 'NSM (Nasjonal sikkerhetsmyndighet) regulations'; Line 128: 'NSM (Nasjonal sikkerhetsmyndighet)' as accreditation authority for Norwegian National Enclave. NSM clearly identified as Norway's national security authority.
Line 53: 'BSI (Bundesamt fur Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik)'; Line 130: 'BSI (in coordination with BMVg)' as accreditation authority for German National Enclave.
Line 52: 'CFCS (Center for Cybersikkerhed)'; Line 129: 'CFCS / FE' as accreditation authority for Danish National Enclave.

Line 57: 'multi-enclave model with a shared NATO SECRET common processing environment, nation-specific enclaves for nationally-classified data'. Lines 127-130 detail separate NOR, DNK, DEU national enclaves plus NATO SECRET Common Domain as shared tier.
Line 723: 'NATO SECRET Common | NATO Type 1 (WAN); TLS 1.3 (LAN) | AES-256 (FIPS 140-3) | NATO KMS / HSM | NATO-approved crypto catalog'. NATO-approved cryptography required for NATO data.

Lines 292-294: CDS (accredited) between NATO SECRET Common and each national enclave. Line 411: 'Every data transfer between security domains must transit an accredited CDS.' Three CDS instances deployed, one per national enclave boundary.
Section 2.5 'Bilateral and Multilateral Agreements Required' with MOU, Technical Arrangement, Security Agreement, and 'Bilateral INFOSEC agreements between each pair of nations' (lines 106-116).

Lines 599-605: Personnel need both national clearance and NATO SECRET clearance. E.g., 'NATO Common Domain | NATO SECRET + project briefing | NATO SECRET clearance from home nation, verified through NPSC'. National enclaves require respective national clearances.

Line 244: 'Cable infrastructure | SDIP-29 | All cabling meets RED/BLACK separation requirements'. Lines 237-244 detail TEMPEST requirements including SDIP-27 Level A/B zones. Section 13.3 covers TEMPEST incident procedures.

Line 127: 'NCIA SAB (NATO Security Accreditation Board) via Norwegian DAA' as accreditation authority for NATO SECRET Common Domain. Line 114: 'NCIA coordination for NATO SECRET network connectivity and accreditation'. Lines 943-945: CDS joint accreditation with NCIA SAB.

Line 18: 'LIST-X Equivalent (Norwegian NSM-approved)'. Line 177: 'facility must be accredited as a LIST-X equivalent under Norwegian NSM regulations'. Section 4 details physical security zones, national cages, TEMPEST requirements, and defense-in-depth model.
